headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from AutoGPT feeding MinerU through shared files/MCP; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent-protocol APIs, while MinerU exposes files and an MCP server. That creates a plausible bridge where AutoGPT-generated content could be ingested by MinerU as trusted document text. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes attacker-controlled text into a file that MinerU later parses
IF MinerU consumes content from a shared MCP or filesystem path without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP access for MinerU during paired runs
Require manual review of any AutoGPT-produced file before MinerU ingests it
Use read-only mounts for MinerU inputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and parser

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, while MinerU is documented as private/fully offline and does not read the filesystem by capability. With no sensitive data classes listed for either agent, leakage is limited unless the operator places secrets into shared files or routes outputs externally.
conditions: IF the operator stores sensitive files in a shared directory
IF AutoGPT is pointed at data that MinerU also processes and then transmits summaries externally
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of any shared workspace
Run AutoGPT with a dedicated output directory
Confirm MinerU remains offline for the session
Review allowlisted egress destinations before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while MinerU supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and multiple instances. Even though MinerU cannot write files or modify git state, both can still contend over shared filesystem resources if co-located, so the conflict is real but not high-severity.
conditions: IF both agents are launched against the same working directory
IF AutoGPT creates or deletes files that MinerU is reading concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same path
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
Use file locks on any shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate intermediate facts or files, and MinerU can ingest documents and OCR text, so MinerU may treat AutoGPT output as authoritative input without a verification step. Because MinerU is a document processor rather than an action-taking agent, the blast radius is usually limited to incorrect downstream documents, not direct external actions.
conditions: IF MinerU processes files produced by AutoGPT without human verification
IF AutoGPT-generated text is used as source material for extracted tables or OCR outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted source material
Compare extracted results against original documents
Limit MinerU to extraction-only runs on vetted inputs
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no handled secrets, no OAuth scopes, and no explicit regulated data classes. The main compliance concern is operational: AutoGPT can egress over allowlisted network paths while MinerU is documented as private/offline, so policy mismatch only appears if the operator routes regulated content through the pair.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through both agents
IF AutoGPT sends extracted content to a remote service while MinerU remains offline-only
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Verify network destinations for AutoGPT
Document retention and deletion handling before use
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
